chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Sarī, from Manṣūr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The thief is one who wages war against Allah and His Messenger, so kill him; and whatever liability comes upon you is upon me.”

key_terms.اللِّصُّ: the thief; the one who steals
key_terms.فَاقْتُلُوهُ: then kill him; an imperative of legal punishment in context
key_terms.فَعَلَيَّ: upon me; meaning responsibility is borne by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.لِرَسُولِهِ: against His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, showing opposition to divinely established authority
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: against Allah, indicating grave religious seriousness
key_terms.مُحَارِبٌ: one who wages war or violent hostility, especially against lawful order

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the legal status of a thief in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the thief as a muharib, one in a state of hostility against Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, within a legal and punitive context. It reflects a severe ruling connected to public order, criminal aggression, and the protection of society and property.
